candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is a stress-induced gastric ulcer. Esophageal varices are a distinct vascular entity typically associated with portal hypertension; the clinical record shows normal liver function tests, normal abdominal ultrasound, and no evidence of portal hypertension or liver disease, making varices an unlikely and incompatible diagnosis. The two entities differ in anatomy, etiology, and pathophysiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Esophageal varices vs. stress-induced gastric ulcer

case_quality_flags: Stress-induced gastric ulcer in a 1-year-old without obvious physiologic stressor is atypical; endoscopic confirmation pending at time of record
